limitations: Anchor adjudication relies on public advisory metadata (OSV, GitHub Advisory Database, NVD CPE range) plus local git ancestry; I did not independently reproduce the CVE with an exploit or a runtime PoC against the built artifact.

The build used go1.27.3, much newer than the go 1.18 directive in go.mod. Build, vet and test-compilation all pass, but the full runtime test suite was not executed, so runtime test behaviour under this toolchain is unverified.
Module resolution depends on public module proxy availability at review time; the build is reproducible only while the pinned versions remain fetchable (go.sum was used unchanged).

The full exported archive is not advisory-id-free: CHANGELOG.md contains CVE-2020-28483 and several GO-* identifiers. Acceptance of the leakage requirement is therefore conditional on the sanitized audit export (123 files, CHANGELOG.md excluded, remaining_advisory_id_count 0) being the evaluation artifact.

The packet's leakage_facts enumerate only CVE/GHSA-style identifiers (cve_id_count 1, ghsa_id_count 0) and do not count the GO-2022-0969, GO-2022-0288, GO-2023-1571 and GO-2022-1144 identifiers that also appear in CHANGELOG.md; this does not change the audit result because the whole file is excluded.

The packet's anchor published_at (2023-05-12T20:19:25Z) is the GHSA publication timestamp; OSV records published 2023-06-08T20:27:15Z and NVD 2023-06-08T21:15:16Z. The affected/fixed facts are unaffected.
discrepancies_observed: Packet anchor published_at is the GitHub Advisory date (2023-05-12T20:19:25Z), whereas OSV and NVD publish the CVE on 2023-06-08; the packet's value matches GHSA exactly, so this is a source-choice difference, not an error in the affected determination.

Packet leakage_facts do not enumerate the four GO-* advisory identifiers present in CHANGELOG.md in addition to CVE-2020-28483; the audit export removes the file entirely, so remaining_advisory_id_count is still 0.
No discrepancies were found in tag resolution, archive/manifest hashes, byte sizes, file counts, tree sha, or per-file content against the git tree.
notes: All required checks 1-5 pass and there is no release-sanity problem, so the verdict is accept. The proposed target is the lightweight tag v1.9.0 at ea03e10384502e1baf6f560a2b0ea32c342ede5b (2023-02-21), whose exported 124-file tree is byte-for-byte identical to the upstream git tree and builds cleanly. CVE-2023-29401 genuinely affects exactly this version (fixed in v1.9.1, commit 4ea0e648; the snapshot is a strict ancestor of the fix and still contains the unescaped FileAttachment header line). The sanitized audit export (123 files, CHANGELOG.md excluded) contains no advisory identifiers. The only caveats are the packet's incomplete GO-* leakage enumeration and the published-date source difference, neither of which affects selection.
